content.title: Explainable, Site-Specific Anomaly Detection for ProtoSense

facts.text: ArmaturaSec reports several terabytes of client captures collected over three years, but no confirmed attack captures. Some clients lacked monitoring, so the company acknowledges that compromise could have gone unnoticed.

sources.quote: we have collected several terabytes of captures from consenting clients over the past three years
we have zero examples of malicious traffic
A few of them have been running their networks for twenty years with no security monitoring at all, so if they were compromised they would not know.

facts.text: ProtoSense covers Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP. ArmaturaSec reports that its previous classifier's false positives caused clients to disable alerts. Its account discusses site-specific baselines and plain-language communication with plant managers.

sources.quote: ProtoSense: passive protocol inspection module for Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP traffic
it flagged so many false positives in real deployments that clients started switching the alerts off.
What we actually need is something that learns what normal looks like on a specific site
We need a method that works with no attack examples and that we can explain to a plant manager in plain language.

facts.text: The company reports hardware for on-device inference and an Embedded Linux, C and Rust environment. Its hardware plan discusses anomaly detection and packet-forwarding latency.

sources.quote: we have the hardware to run inference on-device
Embedded Linux (custom Yocto build)
C and Rust for firmware components
support on-device anomaly detection without affecting packet forwarding latency.

facts.text: ArmaturaSec states a collaboration capacity of one to two part-time engineers and identifies traffic archives, a hardware bench and its firmware codebase within an NDA framework.

sources.quote: We can dedicate one to two engineers part-time to a collaborative project
with access to our traffic archives, our hardware bench, and our existing firmware codebase under NDA.

facts.text: Kiss’s Modbus research models per-register timing, values and command sequences. Her incremental modelling work also tested operator-acknowledged resets after planned process reconfiguration.

sources.quote: For each register address, empirical distributions of inter-request intervals, payload values, and function code sequences were estimated
Concept drift induced by a planned process reconfiguration was detected as a persistent anomaly episode; a supervised reset mechanism based on operator acknowledgement was proposed and tested.

facts.text: Kiss’s group operates an ICS testbed with Modbus/TCP and DNP3 traffic generators. Her notes identify a data-sharing agreement as the framework for industrial testbed access.

sources.quote: The group operates a dedicated ICS testbed equipped with Siemens-compatible PLCs, Modbus/TCP and DNP3 traffic generators, and packet capture infrastructure for long-term dataset collection.
Her group's testbed capacity is available to industrial partners under a data-sharing agreement.

facts.text: Kiss lists joint projects with ICS monitoring companies among her collaboration interests. Her review discusses a false-alarm versus response-latency tradeoff.

sources.quote: joint projects with companies deploying ICS monitoring solutions
the trade-off between false alarm rate and response latency.

inferences: This suggests a practical joint project combining interpretable statistical baselines with one-class modelling. Participation remains conditional because Kiss’s availability is unknown, despite her stated openness to joint projects.
The supplied work does not establish BACnet validity or ProtoSense hardware compatibility. Transfer testing is therefore central; injected scenarios cannot establish real-world attack recall.

Unnoticed compromise could contaminate training, while maintenance could trigger nuisance alerts. Automatic adaptation might absorb persistent attacks; restrictive updates could increase alert burden. The reported false-alarm versus response-latency tradeoff is a deployment risk.
proposedActions: Propose a six-week pilot: ArmaturaSec supplies authorised captures, bench replay and firmware integration; Kiss designs features and evaluation. Separate presumed-normal, unlabelled training, tuning and later held-out periods; verify independence and operating-mode coverage. Compare fixed-threshold rules, statistical baselines and one-class models, training and calibrating without attack labels. Select the best configuration using tuning data, whichever method wins. Evaluate separately for Modbus and BACnet on held-out client replay and controlled bench anomalies, including BACnet commands and legitimate changes. Proposed go/no-go requires the statistical prerequisites below: at least 80% of fully annotated injected episodes detected within 60 seconds; the burden limits below; at least 80% correct plant-manager identification of changed behaviour and appropriate next action; agreed CPU, RAM, storage and throughput limits; and no measurable forwarding-latency increase under representative peak load at agreed resolution. Benchmark the actual Yocto/C/Rust appliance, not presumed hardware fit. Missing protocol data, permissions or sufficient evidence leaves acceptance unresolved.

Propose counting all alert episodes, merging flagged non-overlapping ten-second windows within site/protocol across gaps at most 60 seconds. Require upper 95% day-block-bootstrap bounds of one episode per observed site/protocol-day and, additionally, 1% flagged windows per observed windows, separately per protocol. The latter prevents persistent alerting disappearing through merging. Retain unresolved alerts in both numerators. Predefine sufficient exposure and independent day blocks; insufficient evidence cannot pass. These burden measures use all alerts, not sampled labels.

Randomly sample all evaluation windows uniformly, including non-alert windows, with inclusion probability n/N, for expert review; unresolved labels remain potentially anomalous, not clean. Sampling does not estimate the all-alert burden numerator. Restrict detection claims to fully annotated injected or confirmed cases. Require operator approval for baseline resets and test whether persistent injected anomalies are silently learned away. Negotiate NDA, client permissions and testbed data-sharing terms within the stated part-time capacity before execution.
questions: Can both parties preregister detection scoring separately per protocol: one-to-one matching of each fully annotated injected episode to a new alert beginning within 60 seconds of onset, unmatched episodes counted as misses, and a one-sided 95% lower confidence bound of at least 80%, using independent-run cluster resampling, with minimum runs and episodes fixed beforehand and insufficient evidence unable to pass?

Can representative plant managers undertake explanation testing separately per protocol, scoring each distinct user-case first response as correct only when both changed behaviour and appropriate next action match a preregistered rubric, incomplete answers as failures, repeats excluded, and requiring a one-sided 95% lower confidence bound of at least 80% using user-and-case clustered resampling, with minimum independent users and cases agreed beforehand and insufficient evidence unable to pass?

Can Kiss confirm availability, implementation responsibilities, and a feasible budget and six-week schedule, and can ArmaturaSec nominate expert reviewers and plant managers and confirm or revise the proposed burden, detection-delay and explanation criteria before preregistration?

Which appliance, resource limits, peak traffic conditions and latency measurement resolution will define acceptance, and can authorised captures for both protocols, documented operating changes and BACnet-capable bench equipment be made available under agreed confidentiality and data-sharing terms?

benefits.company: The pilot could establish whether site-specific detection produces manageable, understandable alerts on both protocols without compromising appliance operation, and identify unresolved deployment barriers.
benefits.researcher: Subject to agreement, Kiss could investigate transfer from established Modbus methods to BACnet and operational hardware, using authorised longitudinal captures and controlled bench scenarios to study calibration, drift and explanation quality.

content.markdown:
# Explainable, Site-Specific Anomaly Detection for ProtoSense

## Verified facts
- ArmaturaSec reports several terabytes of client captures collected over three years, but no confirmed attack captures. Some clients lacked monitoring, so the company acknowledges that compromise could have gone unnoticed. [F1]
- ProtoSense covers Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP. ArmaturaSec reports that its previous classifier's false positives caused clients to disable alerts. Its account discusses site-specific baselines and plain-language communication with plant managers. [F2]
- The company reports hardware for on-device inference and an Embedded Linux, C and Rust environment. Its hardware plan discusses anomaly detection and packet-forwarding latency. [F3]
- ArmaturaSec states a collaboration capacity of one to two part-time engineers and identifies traffic archives, a hardware bench and its firmware codebase within an NDA framework. [F4]
- Kiss’s Modbus research models per-register timing, values and command sequences. Her incremental modelling work also tested operator-acknowledged resets after planned process reconfiguration. [F5]
- Kiss’s group operates an ICS testbed with Modbus/TCP and DNP3 traffic generators. Her notes identify a data-sharing agreement as the framework for industrial testbed access. [F6]
- Kiss lists joint projects with ICS monitoring companies among her collaboration interests. Her review discusses a false-alarm versus response-latency tradeoff. [F7]

## Potential benefits
- For the company: The pilot could establish whether site-specific detection produces manageable, understandable alerts on both protocols without compromising appliance operation, and identify unresolved deployment barriers.
- For the researcher: Subject to agreement, Kiss could investigate transfer from established Modbus methods to BACnet and operational hardware, using authorised longitudinal captures and controlled bench scenarios to study calibration, drift and explanation quality.

## Our inference
- This suggests a practical joint project combining interpretable statistical baselines with one-class modelling. Participation remains conditional because Kiss’s availability is unknown, despite her stated openness to joint projects.
- The supplied work does not establish BACnet validity or ProtoSense hardware compatibility. Transfer testing is therefore central; injected scenarios cannot establish real-world attack recall.
- Unnoticed compromise could contaminate training, while maintenance could trigger nuisance alerts. Automatic adaptation might absorb persistent attacks; restrictive updates could increase alert burden. The reported false-alarm versus response-latency tradeoff is a deployment risk.

## Proposed next steps
- Propose a six-week pilot: ArmaturaSec supplies authorised captures, bench replay and firmware integration; Kiss designs features and evaluation. Separate presumed-normal, unlabelled training, tuning and later held-out periods; verify independence and operating-mode coverage. Compare fixed-threshold rules, statistical baselines and one-class models, training and calibrating without attack labels. Select the best configuration using tuning data, whichever method wins. Evaluate separately for Modbus and BACnet on held-out client replay and controlled bench anomalies, including BACnet commands and legitimate changes. Proposed go/no-go requires the statistical prerequisites below: at least 80% of fully annotated injected episodes detected within 60 seconds; the burden limits below; at least 80% correct plant-manager identification of changed behaviour and appropriate next action; agreed CPU, RAM, storage and throughput limits; and no measurable forwarding-latency increase under representative peak load at agreed resolution. Benchmark the actual Yocto/C/Rust appliance, not presumed hardware fit. Missing protocol data, permissions or sufficient evidence leaves acceptance unresolved.
- Propose counting all alert episodes, merging flagged non-overlapping ten-second windows within site/protocol across gaps at most 60 seconds. Require upper 95% day-block-bootstrap bounds of one episode per observed site/protocol-day and, additionally, 1% flagged windows per observed windows, separately per protocol. The latter prevents persistent alerting disappearing through merging. Retain unresolved alerts in both numerators. Predefine sufficient exposure and independent day blocks; insufficient evidence cannot pass. These burden measures use all alerts, not sampled labels.
- Randomly sample all evaluation windows uniformly, including non-alert windows, with inclusion probability n/N, for expert review; unresolved labels remain potentially anomalous, not clean. Sampling does not estimate the all-alert burden numerator. Restrict detection claims to fully annotated injected or confirmed cases. Require operator approval for baseline resets and test whether persistent injected anomalies are silently learned away. Negotiate NDA, client permissions and testbed data-sharing terms within the stated part-time capacity before execution.

## Open questions
- Can both parties preregister detection scoring separately per protocol: one-to-one matching of each fully annotated injected episode to a new alert beginning within 60 seconds of onset, unmatched episodes counted as misses, and a one-sided 95% lower confidence bound of at least 80%, using independent-run cluster resampling, with minimum runs and episodes fixed beforehand and insufficient evidence unable to pass?
- Can representative plant managers undertake explanation testing separately per protocol, scoring each distinct user-case first response as correct only when both changed behaviour and appropriate next action match a preregistered rubric, incomplete answers as failures, repeats excluded, and requiring a one-sided 95% lower confidence bound of at least 80% using user-and-case clustered resampling, with minimum independent users and cases agreed beforehand and insufficient evidence unable to pass?
- Can Kiss confirm availability, implementation responsibilities, and a feasible budget and six-week schedule, and can ArmaturaSec nominate expert reviewers and plant managers and confirm or revise the proposed burden, detection-delay and explanation criteria before preregistration?
- Which appliance, resource limits, peak traffic conditions and latency measurement resolution will define acceptance, and can authorised captures for both protocols, documented operating changes and BACnet-capable bench equipment be made available under agreed confidentiality and data-sharing terms?

content.title: Joint project: reliable Serbian support search across scripts and word forms

facts.text: LinguaBot reports that about 18% of 12,000 real support queries from one bank client returned no useful result; its analysis attributed more than half of those misses to morphological mismatch or script confusion.

sources.quote: in a sample of 12,000 real support queries from one bank client, about 18% returned no useful result
our analysis traced more than half of those misses directly to morphological mismatch or script confusion.

facts.text: The company describes an Elasticsearch baseline using a Croatian-built stemmer, within-word script mixing, and manual synonym maintenance that does not scale with quarterly terminology changes.

sources.quote: Our current Elasticsearch setup uses a basic stemmer that was built for Croatian
our users freely switch between Latin and Cyrillic script mid-sentence — sometimes mid-word in typos.
maintaining those lists manually does not scale as clients add new product terminology every quarter.

facts.text: LinguaBot reports around 85,000 labelled query-response pairs across all clients and two in-house linguists able to annotate or validate solutions.

sources.quote: We have a labelled query-response dataset of around 85,000 pairs across all clients
our two in-house linguists can annotate or validate proposed solutions.

facts.text: LinguaBot identifies approximately EUR 8,000 as its tooling/data budget. Its stated success criteria concern miss rate, maintenance and vocabulary updates.

sources.quote: Budget for tooling or data work is modest — around 8,000 EUR — and we want something testable within six months.
A good outcome is getting that 18% miss rate below 5% and keeping it there with a manageable maintenance process.
can be updated when new vocabulary arrives without a full re-index.

facts.text: Dragić’s research maps tokens to phoneme sequences for script canonicalization. His morphological-reduction study investigates interactions between stemming, lemmatization and script normalization.

sources.quote: This paper presents a token canonicalization procedure in which each token is mapped to a phoneme sequence
U ovom radu ispitujemo kako stemovanje i lematizacija interaguju s postupkom normalizacije skripte pri izgradnji pretražnog indeksa.

facts.text: Dragić reports two active projects and capacity for one smaller industrial contract or consultancy, with no interest in general software development lacking a research component.

sources.quote: Trenutno je angažovan na dva aktivna projekta, ali ima kapaciteta za jedan manji industrijski ugovor ili konsultantski angažman.
nije zainteresovan za opšte projekte razvoja softvera bez istraživačke komponente.

facts.text: His neural-transliteration evidence reports a tradeoff: regular-token character error was higher for the transformer than deterministic rules, despite improvement on exceptions.

sources.quote: The transformer model achieved a character error rate of 0.4% on regular tokens and 3.1% on the exception classes,
compared with 0.1% and 19.4% respectively for the deterministic baseline.

inferences: This suggests a focused joint project on normalization interactions rather than general product development. Participation is conditional: joint-project willingness is open, but Dragić’s actual availability and allocation remain unconfirmed and limited in scope.

Legal and benchmark evidence does not validate short banking or telecom queries, within-word typos, or vocabulary-rule changes without re-indexing. Incremental document insertion is not equivalent to updating rules against existing content.
Normalization may address only part of the miss rate. Exception handling could introduce errors or maintenance burdens, so the best configuration may be simpler than a neural pipeline.
proposedActions: Propose eight configurations: existing Elasticsearch baseline; script canonicalization, Serbian morphological normalization and incremental vocabulary handling individually; every pair; and all three. Predefine independent on/off factor levels; hold corpus, ranking and queries constant. Split the 85,000 pairs into tuning and held-out evaluation samples; verify independence, preventing query, answer-template and client leakage. Select the best configuration on tuning data. Linguists would judge every evaluation occurrence at an agreed cutoff. Miss rate counts occurrences with no useful result divided by all evaluated occurrences, without deduplication; unresolved judgments count as misses. Proposed go/no-go: upper 95% confidence bound below 5% separately for the original bank-client population, initially and after updates; separate pre-agreed gates for telecom, within-word mixing and unseen terminology; no full re-index; agreed maintenance and latency caps under production load; prototype testable within six months and approximately EUR 8,000 tooling/data expenditure. Missing or insufficient evidence means no pass. A factor’s isolated null effect does not end interaction testing.

Before tuning, agree separate miss-rate ceilings and upper-95%-bound acceptance rules for representative held-out telecom queries and real within-word-mixing/new-vocabulary strata, initially and after updates; pooled success cannot substitute. Keep constructed typo probes separate, with their own pre-agreed acceptance rule, not automatically the bank’s 5% target. Establish corpus access and usable judgments. Replay terminology updates against existing indexed documents, recording operations, retrieval changes, maintenance hours and latency. Unavailable evaluation data or unresolved acceptance rules block a pass.

Propose month one for permissions, baseline reproduction and protocol agreement; months two through four for integration and tuning; months five through six for locked evaluation and update replay. LinguaBot would supply engineering and linguist validation; Dragić would guide canonicalization, morphological comparisons and error analysis, subject to his allocation. Test banking/telecom terminology, foreign names, abbreviations and alphanumeric identifiers explicitly. Validate Elasticsearch compatibility and update behavior rather than assuming prior implementations transfer.
questions: Can Dragić confirm availability, start timing and allocation for this small research-focused joint project, with a named company engineering counterpart?

Can LinguaBot authorize anonymized query-response pairs, corresponding knowledge-base documents and usable relevance judgments, including independent held-out data from the original bank-client population, telecom queries and the required real-error strata?

What cutoff defines a useful result, is below 5% the prototype acceptance target, and what separate telecom, mixing, new-vocabulary and constructed-probe acceptance rules, production load, hardware and latency cap should govern evaluation?

Which Elasticsearch version and update mechanisms are permitted without a full re-index, what maintenance-hours cap is acceptable, and how are researcher fees and annotation effort funded beyond the tooling/data allocation?

benefits.company: The experiment could identify which components reduce actual support-search misses and whether terminology updates remain practical without rebuilding the index.
benefits.researcher: Subject to agreement and authorized access, Dragić could test normalization interactions on industrial support queries and study transfer beyond legal and benchmark retrieval.

content.title: Explaining chilled-store conveyor weld cracking

facts.text: AutomVoj reports cracking after about 18 months at main crossmember-to-stringer connections in painted mild-steel hollow-section frames. Its room-temperature loaded workshop tests have not reproduced the failure.

sources.quote: Our conveyor frames are welded from mild steel hollow section and painted for corrosion resistance before delivery.
we are seeing weld joint cracking at the main crossmember-to-stringer connections after about 18 months of continuous use.
We test frames under load at room temperature and they pass without any problem.

facts.text: The company describes cold-store operation at 2–6 °C and suspects interacting thermal cycling, condensation and loaded-belt vibration; it does not report established causal roles.

sources.quote: typically operating between 2 °C and 6 °C
Our suspicion is that the combination of thermal cycling, condensation, and the vibration load from loaded belts

facts.text: AutomVoj has site photographs and crack measurements, but only two retained failed sections.

sources.quote: We have photos and measurements of the cracked joints from site visits, and we still have two of the failed sections in storage.

facts.text: AutomVoj lacks low-temperature cyclic-load testing equipment and know-how. Erić’s climate chamber and servo-hydraulic machine are shared with two other research groups.

sources.quote: We do not currently have the equipment or know-how to test at low temperatures under cyclic load.
Erić's climate chamber and servo-hydraulic machine are shared with two other research groups; scheduling access for extended test campaigns requires advance coordination.

facts.text: AutomVoj has no dedicated R&D department; its chief engineer and two senior automation engineers divide their time between live projects and improvement work.

sources.quote: We have no dedicated R&D department
our chief engineer and two senior automation engineers who allocate time between live projects and improvement work.

facts.text: Erić’s published work examined mechanical fatigue combined with thermal cycling in butt-welded S275JR plates between −30 °C and +20 °C. It reported crack growth exceeding simple mechanical-plus-thermal predictions.

sources.quote: superimposed thermal cycling (between −30 °C and +20 °C at 0.5 cycles per hour) during mechanical fatigue loading
in butt-welded S275JR plates.
Crack growth rates in both TMF programmes exceeded predictions based on simple superposition of mechanical and thermal stress intensities

facts.text: Erić lists openness to joint projects involving low-temperature or combined-loading fatigue testing.

sources.quote: joint projects involving fatigue testing under low-temperature or combined loading conditions

inferences: This suggests a relevant joint project, conditional on Erić’s unknown availability and AutomVoj’s agreement. Openness does not establish a commitment or equipment booking.

Transfer remains unvalidated: colder plate tests do not establish the mechanism in painted hollow-section joints at 2–6 °C. Condensation control and corrosion expertise may require additional support; accelerated loading could produce irrelevant fractures and cannot alone establish an 18-month service life.
proposedActions: Propose production-representative painted crossmember-to-stringer specimens: AutomVoj would contribute fabrication records, specimens and service measurements; Erić would lead examination and testing, subject to agreement. Independently define thermal cycling (steady 2–6 °C chilled condition versus measured excursions), condensation (dry versus controlled wetting) and vibration (absent versus measured spectrum). Hold static belt load, weld condition and coating comparable. Test baseline, each factor alone, all pairs and the full combination, plus the room-temperature workshop reference. Separate tuning from held-out evaluation specimens and verify independence. Measure cycles to a predefined detectable crack, growth, origin and morphology. Select the best-supported condition on tuning data. Proposed reproduction gate: at least two of three held-out replicates must match the field failure under the frozen rubric and exposure window, with measured exposures reproduced and uncertainty reported. Ambiguous matches and specimens without matching cracks by the window’s end do not count. Mechanism support additionally requires the held-out contrasts below; otherwise reproduction is inconclusive. An inactive single factor never excludes interactions.

Propose two weeks for evidence review and instrumentation planning, then six weeks of testing after advance equipment booking; renegotiate against measured service cycles. Before held-out testing, freeze a field-informed rubric specifying connection location, origin, morphology and tolerances, ambiguous-match handling, and exposure/censoring window. Preserve failed material through non-destructive documentation and an agreed sampling map. Confirm representative-specimen fit, independent moisture control, safe operation and engineering allocation before manufacture; insufficient evidence to freeze these prerequisites blocks evaluation.

Prespecify held-out main-effect and interaction contrasts, meaningful-effect bounds and simultaneous 95% confidence intervals. Support a factor explanation only when a contrast interval lies wholly beyond its negligible-effect band; indistinguishable conditions or insufficient precision remain inconclusive. After both gates pass, use calibrated modelling to tune welding, filler or geometry changes. Evaluate the best configuration independently against unchanged production joints under reproduced exposures, using pre-agreed adoption criteria and welding requirements. Warranty reduction remains a longer-term field-validation question.
questions: Can Erić confirm availability and bookable facilities, and can AutomVoj confirm participation in this joint-project format?
What budget, decision deadline and engineering time can AutomVoj allocate?

Can AutomVoj authorise limited destructive sampling, provide fabrication and coating records, and arrange representative strain, vibration, belt-load, temperature and humidity measurements covering starts, stops, washdown and defrost?
What modification-adoption evidence, meaningful factorial-effect bounds and applicable design or welding requirements should be agreed before testing?

benefits.company: The first comparison could distinguish individual and interacting service factors and provide a defensible basis for changing the joint rather than relying on room-temperature tests alone.
benefits.researcher: Subject to agreement and access, Erić could test transfer of thermo-mechanical fatigue methods to coated hollow-section conveyor joints using service measurements, failed-section evidence and controlled comparisons.
